items.title: US economy roars ahead in third quarter, inflation remains high in October By Reuters
items.excerpt: Spending is being driven mostly by higher-income households, whose wealth was boosted by the stock market before the ongoing AI-led selloff. Economists expect consumer spending to slow to a still-healthy pace in the fourth quarter, though declining gasoline prices should ease some of the financial pressure on middle- and lower-income households. Average retail gasoline prices have dropped below $4 a gallon for the first time since mid-July, data from the US Energy Information Administration showed. ... The Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index increased 0.3% in October after gaining 0.5% in September, the BEA said. PCE inflation was lifted by higher prices for goods, including food and household furnishings, as well as services such as recreation, dining out and hotel stays. In the 12 months through October, PCE inflation increased 3.8% after advancing 3.6% in September. Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the PCE Price Index increased 0.3% for the third straight month. So-called core PCE inflation increased 3.3% on a year-over-year basis in October, the largest advance since November 2023, after climbing 3.1% in September. The Fed tracks the PCE price measures for its 2% inflation target.

In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased. Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending. For more information, refer to the " Technical Notes" below. Compared to the second quarter, the acceleration in real GDP in the third quarter primarily reflected an acceleration in investment and an upturn in government spending that were partly offset by a downturn in exports. Imports increased more in the third quarter than in the second quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, the sum of consumer spending and gross private fixed investment, increased 5.8 percent in the third quarter, revised up 0.9 percentage point from the previous estimate. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7 percent in the third quarter, revised down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index increased 2.1 percent, and the PCE price index, excluding food and energy increased 2.5 percent, both the same as previously estimated. Real gross domestic income (GDI) increased 4.4 percent in the third quarter, compared with an increase of 2.3 percent (revised) in the second quarter. items.title: Judge blocks latest Trump effort to restrict birthright citizenship - ABC News
items.excerpt: A federal judge in Washington, D.C., on Wednesday blocked the Trump administration's latest effort to restrict birthright citizenship for the children of international workers born in the United States, according to a newly filed ruling. D.C. District Judge Christopher Cooper, an appointee of former President Barack Obama, granted a request for a preliminary injunction blocking President Donald Trump's executive order earlier this year that came in the wake of the Supreme Court's ruling that struck down Trump's push to formally end birthright citizenship. ... Trump aimed to do away with birthright citizenship altogether in an executive order he signed on the first day of his second term last year. In August, he signed another executive order targeting birthright citizenship -- one that would outlaw what the administration has described as "birth tourism" and another that would narrow the criteria for who is eligible for birthright citizenship. The narrower executive order directed federal agencies to not grant citizenship to children born in the U.S. to parents that lacked diplomatic immunity and who worked for foreign governments or other organizations, those born through commercial surrogacy, as well as children with a parent who is a suspected gang member or potential terrorist. But in his ruling, Cooper said Trump "cannot carve out new exceptions to birthright citizenship for children born within the United States and subject to its laws" and granted the request for an injunction and class-action status from a group that filed suit who claimed their citizenship would be unlawfully denied if the order was implemented. "The Citizenship Clause promises citizenship to practically all children born in the United States," Cooper said in the ruling. "Earlier this year, the Supreme Court kept that promise by striking down EO1. This Court does so again today by enjoining EO2’s application as to the certified class."

items.title: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt settle winery fight lawsuit that surfaced abuse allegations
items.excerpt: Nov. 25, 2026, 8:06 PM EST / Source: The Associated Press By The Associated Press The long-running legal battles between Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt have come to an end a decade after the A-list celebrity couple split, with the actors settling a dispute over the ownership of a French winery. The actors said in a joint statement Wednesday that they had reached a settlement of the lawsuit, which transcended business matters when a legal filing from Jolie surfaced abuse allegations against Pitt. “We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further,” the statement provided by representatives for Pitt, 62, and Jolie, 51, said. Jolie filed for divorce in 2016, citing the “health of the family,” after a private jet flight from Europe. The couple’s use of private judges — an ... But the winery lawsuit became a way for details of their dispute to become public. Pitt sued Jolie in 2022, saying she had abandoned an agreement that he would buy her half of Chateau Miraval, a French winery they owned together. She instead sold her part to the Tenute del Mondo wine group. Pitt said it was a “vindictive” and “unlawful” move that should not have been made without his consent and ruined a private space that had been a second home. The descriptions of the abuse alleged on the private flight weren’t public until Jolie filed a cross-complaint in the dispute. Jolie and her attorneys said Pitt had demanded she sign a wide-ranging nondisclosure agreement about him as part of the proposed deal that was an attempt to cover up his abuse of her and the children. The FBI and child services officials had investigated Pitt’s actions on the flight, centering on the treatment of their eldest son. The FBI released a statement in late 2016 saying it would not investigate further, and the U.S. attorney did not bring charges. Pitt has denied being abusive but did not defend his behavior on the flight.
